nodes.title: Compute services: Key Ideas
nodes.content: 'Compute' is everything that runs your code: VMs, containers, serverless functions, batch jobs. The exam wants you to pick the right shape — long-running stateful workload → VM, packaged app → container, event-driven short job → serverless.

flashcards.front: VM vs container vs serverless — pick a service for each.
flashcards.back: VM (EC2 / Compute Engine / Azure VM) when you need full OS control. Container (ECS, GKE, AKS, Cloud Run) when you've packaged an app and want orchestration. Serverless (Lambda, Functions, Cloud Functions) for short event-driven tasks, no infrastructure to manage.

A service that adds/removes compute instances based on a signal (CPU, request rate, queue depth, custom metric). Scale-out is cheap; scale-in saves money. Target tracking is the simplest mode: 'keep average CPU at 60%'.

flashcards.front: Spot / preemptible / low-priority — what's the catch?
flashcards.back: Up to 90% off list price, but the cloud can yank the instance with 30 s – 2 min warning. Use for fault-tolerant batch jobs, CI runners, big-data clusters. Don't use for stateful databases or anything that needs to stay up.
On-demand: pay by the hour or second, no commitment. Reserved / committed: 1-3 year commitment, 30-60% discount, no flexibility. Pick reserved for steady baseline load, on-demand for spiky workloads.

questions.q: A CFO is reviewing the move from on-premises servers to Google Cloud and asks which property of the cloud model converts large hardware purchases into ongoing operating expenses. Which characteristic best explains this shift?
choices: Cloud providers contractually fix a flat monthly fee per workload that holds steady for the full multi-year contract term
Cloud workloads automatically relocate to whichever region offers the lowest spot price at the precise moment of execution
Cloud resources are billed for actual consumption rather than purchased upfront as fixed long-lived hardware capital assets
Cloud providers price per-server hardware below what private datacenter operators typically achieve at comparable scale and volume
questions.explanation: The cloud's pay-as-you-go consumption model converts large up-front CapEx (servers, datacenter build-out, hardware refresh cycles) into variable OpEx tied to actual usage. Flat per-workload monthly fees are not how consumption pricing works; automatic spot relocation across regions is not a default behaviour; and per-server price comparisons vary by workload and do not by themselves shift CapEx to OpEx.

questions.q: A retail analyst needs to run interactive SQL against a 50 TB clickstream dataset stored in Google Cloud, with no servers to manage and per-query or capacity-based billing. Which Google Cloud service is the best fit for this workload?
choices: Cloud Spanner, a globally distributed relational database that supports strongly consistent ACID transactions across multiple regions
BigQuery, a serverless petabyte-scale data warehouse designed for fast analytical SQL on multi-terabyte to petabyte datasets
Cloud SQL, a managed relational database service intended primarily for OLTP workloads on a single primary instance with read replicas
Bigtable, a wide-column NoSQL store optimised for very low-latency single-key reads and writes on dense time-series data
questions.explanation: BigQuery is Google Cloud's serverless analytics warehouse, built for ad-hoc SQL on multi-terabyte to petabyte datasets without provisioning infrastructure; it bills per bytes scanned (on-demand) or by reserved slots (capacity). Cloud Spanner is a globally consistent transactional database; Cloud SQL targets OLTP at a much smaller scale with row-by-row processing; Bigtable is a NoSQL key-value store, not an analytical SQL engine.

questions.q: A company must retain regulatory archives for at least seven years. The data will be accessed only during occasional audits, perhaps once per year. Which Cloud Storage class minimises monthly storage cost for this access pattern?
choices: Standard storage, intended for frequently accessed hot data and priced higher per GB than every colder Cloud Storage class
Nearline storage, designed for data read on average about once per month at a lower storage rate than the Standard class
Coldline storage, intended for data accessed roughly once per quarter and priced lower than Nearline for that infrequent pattern
Archive storage, the lowest-cost Cloud Storage class for data retained long term and read at most once a year for compliance
questions.explanation: Archive is the cheapest Cloud Storage class per GB-month and is designed for data accessed at most once per year, such as long-term regulatory archives. Standard fits hot data and costs the most per GB; Nearline targets ~monthly access; Coldline targets ~quarterly access. Each colder class also has higher retrieval and minimum-storage-duration charges, which only pay off for low-access archival use.

questions.q: A bank wants to deploy a custom fraud-detection model that data scientists train in notebooks and product teams call as a managed online endpoint. Which Google Cloud platform unifies training, deployment, and monitoring of custom ML models?
choices: Vertex AI, the unified ML platform for building, training, tuning, deploying, and monitoring custom machine-learning models in one product
Document AI, a service that extracts structured fields from invoices, receipts, contracts, and other semi-structured business documents
Apigee, a full-lifecycle API management platform for publishing, securing, monitoring, throttling, and monetising APIs to external consumers
Looker, a business intelligence and embedded analytics platform that builds governed dashboards on top of SQL data warehouses
questions.explanation: Vertex AI is Google Cloud's unified ML platform: it covers data preparation, notebook training (Workbench), AutoML, custom training, model registry, online and batch prediction endpoints, and model monitoring under one product. Document AI extracts fields from documents; Apigee manages APIs; Looker is a BI and visualisation tool — none of them train and serve a custom ML model end-to-end.

questions.q: A small team wants to run a stateless containerised web service that scales to zero when idle and bills only per request. They do not want to manage clusters or VMs. Which Google Cloud service fits this requirement most directly?
choices: Compute Engine, which provisions persistent virtual machines that the customer scales, patches, and pays for continuously while they run
Cloud Spanner, a globally distributed managed relational database that scales horizontally for high-throughput transactional workloads
Google Kubernetes Engine, a managed cluster service that runs containerised workloads on a customer-sized pool of standing worker nodes
Cloud Run, a fully managed serverless platform that runs stateless containers, scales them to zero when idle, and bills per request
questions.explanation: Cloud Run runs stateless containers on a fully managed serverless platform: it can scale to zero instances when there is no traffic and bills per request (CPU and memory time per request). Compute Engine VMs run continuously and are billed for idle time; GKE bills for the underlying node VMs even when pods are idle; Cloud Spanner is a database, not a container runtime.

questions.q: An engineering team already packages services as Docker images and wants Kubernetes-native orchestration with a managed control plane, autoscaling node pools, and integrated Google Cloud networking. Which service should they choose?
choices: App Engine Standard, a sandboxed platform-as-a-service that runs framework-restricted applications on a fully managed runtime with built-in autoscaling
Google Kubernetes Engine, a managed Kubernetes service with a Google-operated control plane, autoscaling worker node pools, and VPC integration
Cloud Functions, an event-driven serverless service that runs short-lived function code in response to HTTP, Pub/Sub, and storage triggers
Bare Metal Solution, dedicated single-tenant physical hardware in a Google datacenter for legacy on-premises database workloads such as Oracle
questions.explanation: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) is Google's managed Kubernetes service: it runs the control plane on the customer's behalf, supports autoscaling node pools, and integrates with VPC networking, IAM, and Cloud Operations. App Engine Standard abstracts the cluster entirely and does not expose a Kubernetes API; Cloud Functions is an event-driven FaaS, not a Kubernetes orchestrator; Bare Metal Solution targets legacy enterprise databases on bare hardware.

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

questions.q: A company plans to move a 15-year-old Java application to Google Cloud with the least possible code change first, then refactor later. The application currently runs on physical Linux servers in their datacenter. Which initial migration strategy fits this?
choices: Refactor (re-architect) the application into microservices on Google Kubernetes Engine before moving any of its production traffic to the cloud
Rebuild the application from scratch as a serverless workload on Cloud Run and decommission the previous Java codebase entirely on cutover
Replace the existing application entirely with a Google Workspace SaaS equivalent and migrate the end users onto the new SaaS product
Rehost (lift-and-shift) the application onto Compute Engine virtual machines first and modernise the architecture iteratively in a later phase
questions.explanation: Rehost (lift-and-shift) is the migration strategy with the smallest immediate code change: the workload moves to Compute Engine VMs that resemble the existing servers, deferring re-architecture. Refactor and rebuild both require significant rework up front; replace abandons the existing application. A common pattern is rehost first to capture cloud benefits quickly, then iteratively refactor toward containers or managed services.

questions.q: A CISO reviews who is accountable for what under Google Cloud's shared responsibility model for an IaaS workload running on Compute Engine virtual machines. Which statement best describes the division of responsibility for that workload?
choices: Google secures the physical infrastructure and the hypervisor; the customer secures the guest OS, applications, and data inside the VM
Google secures everything from hardware through the customer's own application code, including OS patches that customer teams apply inside the VM
The customer is responsible for the physical security of the regional Google datacenters that host the virtual machines they provision
Google is responsible for the customer's IAM role assignments and the configuration of every project firewall rule the customer authors
questions.explanation: Under shared responsibility on IaaS (Compute Engine), Google secures the lower layers — physical hardware, datacenter, network, and the hypervisor — while the customer is responsible for the guest OS (including patches), middleware, applications, identity configuration, network rules they author, and their data. Google does not patch guest OS images; customers never own datacenter physical security; and IAM and firewall policy are always the customer's decision.

questions.q: A platform engineer needs to grant a deployment service account permission to publish messages to a single Pub/Sub topic, and nothing else. Which Google Cloud IAM approach lets them grant this least-privilege access most precisely?
choices: A Cloud KMS customer-managed encryption key shared with the topic so that messages from the service account decrypt at the subscriber side correctly
A predefined or custom IAM role bound to the service account on that specific Pub/Sub topic resource, granting only publisher permission
An IP allow-list on the project's default VPC firewall that permits the service account's outbound traffic toward the Pub/Sub API endpoint
An organisation-wide Owner role granted to the service account so it can act across every project in the organisation that hosts topics
questions.explanation: Google Cloud IAM lets you bind a role to a principal (such as a service account) at a specific resource — for Pub/Sub, that includes the individual topic. Granting roles/pubsub.publisher on just that topic gives the minimum needed publish permission and nothing else. Owner at the org root grants broad authority and breaks least privilege; firewall rules govern network reachability, not API authorisation; KMS handles encryption keys, not API permission.

questions.q: An SRE team needs centralised metrics, logs, traces, and alerts for workloads running across Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run, without standing up a separate observability stack. Which Google Cloud product set provides this?
choices: Cloud Source Repositories and Cloud Code, which host private Git repositories and provide IDE plugins for development inside VS Code and JetBrains
Cloud Deployment Manager and Cloud Build for declaring infrastructure templates in YAML and running container build and test pipelines automatically
Cloud Operations suite — Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Trace — for unified metrics, log aggregation, distributed tracing, and alerts
Cloud Asset Inventory and Recommender for tracking resource configuration state, change history, and surfacing right-sizing recommendations across projects
questions.explanation: Google Cloud Operations (formerly Stackdriver) bundles Cloud Monitoring (metrics, dashboards, alerting), Cloud Logging (centralised log aggregation and queries), and Cloud Trace (distributed tracing) across Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run, and other services with built-in agents. Source Repositories and Cloud Code are for source control and IDE tooling; Deployment Manager and Cloud Build handle IaC and CI; Asset Inventory and Recommender focus on configuration state and right-sizing, not application telemetry.

questions.q: A multinational retailer must keep certain customer records physically stored only in the European Union to satisfy a data-residency obligation. Which Google Cloud capability lets them control the geographic location where their data is stored?
choices: Choosing the region or multi-region when creating resources such as Cloud Storage buckets and BigQuery datasets controls where that data is stored
Google Cloud automatically replicates every customer's data across every region worldwide for maximum durability, so residency cannot be customer-constrained
Data residency for resources is governed solely by the billing account's country of registration and cannot be changed once the organisation has been created
Only the Premium Network Service Tier can pin data to a specific country at rest; the Standard Tier always stores data in a global pool transparently
questions.explanation: Customers control data location by selecting a region (for example europe-west1) or a regional or multi-region scope (for example the EU multi-region) when creating storage and data resources; Google does not move that data outside the chosen location. Google does not silently replicate all data to every region; the billing account's country does not dictate resource location; and Network Service Tiers govern traffic routing and egress price, not where data is stored at rest.

questions.q: A logistics company wants to add a chatbot to its website that understands customer questions in natural language and replies conversationally, without building and training a model from scratch. Which Google Cloud offering most directly addresses this need?
choices: Cloud Composer, a managed Apache Airflow service for authoring and orchestrating multi-step data pipelines and ML workflow DAGs at scale
BigQuery ML, so analysts can train and serve forecasting, classification, and clustering models using familiar SQL statements against warehouse tables
A conversational AI product such as Dialogflow or Vertex AI Agent Builder that provides ready-made natural-language understanding for chatbots
Cloud Data Fusion, a graphical drag-and-drop tool for building and managing ETL and ELT data integration jobs without writing transformation code
questions.explanation: Conversational AI products such as Dialogflow and Vertex AI Agent Builder provide pre-built natural-language understanding and dialogue management, letting a business deploy a chatbot without training its own model. Cloud Composer orchestrates workflows; BigQuery ML trains analytical models in SQL but is not a dialogue engine; Cloud Data Fusion builds ETL pipelines — none deliver a turnkey natural-language chatbot.

nodes.title: Network operations (CompTIA Network+): Key Ideas
nodes.content: Network+ tests operational fundamentals: how SNMP works for device monitoring, why baseline documentation matters, the change-management process that prevents accidental outages, and syslog severity levels that tell you how serious a message is. These appear in scenario questions where you're asked which tool to use or which process was skipped.

flashcards.front: SNMP — OID, MIB, community string, v2c vs v3.
flashcards.back: OID (Object Identifier): a dotted-number path in the MIB tree that uniquely identifies one piece of device data (e.g., `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10` = ifInOctets). MIB (Management Information Base): the schema/dictionary that maps OIDs to human-readable names. Community string: a plain-text password used for SNMP v1/v2c authentication — typically 'public' (read) and 'private' (write); a well-known security weakness. SNMPv3 replaces community strings with proper user-based auth (MD5/SHA) and encryption (AES/DES).

flashcards.front: Why is network baseline documentation critical?
flashcards.back: A baseline records normal traffic volumes, CPU/memory levels, error rates, and routing tables — captured during a known-good period. When something goes wrong, you compare current readings to the baseline to spot the anomaly (utilization spiked 300%, a new route appeared, error rate tripled). Without a baseline, 'high CPU' is meaningless because you don't know what 'normal' was. Network+ expects you to identify baselining as a best practice before troubleshooting.

flashcards.front: Change management process — what are the key steps?
flashcards.back: Request change → assess risk and impact → obtain approval (CAB or manager) → schedule a maintenance window → implement → test and verify → document outcome → close. The exam distinguishes emergency changes (faster approval path for critical incidents) from standard changes (pre-approved, low-risk, routine). Skipping change management is the most common cause of self-inflicted outages.

0 Emergency, 1 Alert, 2 Critical, 3 Error, 4 Warning, 5 Notice, 6 Informational, 7 Debug. Lower number = more severe. Most organizations alert on 0–3 and log 0–6. Debug (7) produces enormous volume and is usually enabled only during active troubleshooting. The mnemonic: Every Awful Crisis Erodes Wisdom, No Debate.

questions.q: An operations manager is told that a critical customer-facing API must stay available even if an entire Google Cloud zone fails. Which deployment approach best improves availability against a single zone outage?
choices: Run every API instance in a single zone but enable Cloud CDN at the edge so cached responses keep serving traffic and absorb the zone outage entirely
Increase the machine type of the single VM to the largest available size with the highest sustained CPU performance so it is less likely to fail under load
Store more frequent snapshots of the boot disk so the failed instance can be quickly restored as soon as the zone has finished recovering
Distribute the workload across multiple zones in the region behind a load balancer so a single zone failure removes only part of the capacity
questions.explanation: Spreading instances across multiple zones in a region, behind a load balancer, means a single zone outage removes only part of the capacity while the service keeps serving from the healthy zones — the standard high-availability pattern. Cloud CDN only caches static or cacheable content and cannot serve a fully dynamic API during an outage; a bigger single VM is still a single point of failure in one zone; and snapshots speed recovery after the fact but do not keep the service available during the outage.

questions.q: A finance team wants to be alerted automatically when monthly Google Cloud spending is on track to exceed a planned threshold, so they can react before the bill arrives. Which Cloud Billing feature should they use?
choices: A Cloud Billing budget with configurable alert thresholds that emails stakeholders when actual or forecasted spend crosses the configured percentage threshold
Committed use discounts, which lower the rate paid for sustained Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run usage over a one- or three-year capacity commitment
The Google Cloud pricing calculator, which estimates the monthly cost of a proposed architecture before any resources are actually deployed in the project
Billing account currency conversion settings, which restate the monthly invoice total into the organisation's local accounting currency for finance reports
questions.explanation: Cloud Billing budgets let you set a budget amount and alert thresholds (for example 50 / 90 / 100 percent) that trigger notifications on actual or forecasted spend, giving early warning before the bill is final. Committed use discounts reduce the unit price but do not alert on spend; the pricing calculator only produces pre-deployment estimates; and currency conversion just restates totals — none of those provide proactive overspend alerts.

questions.q: A leadership team is debating whether to commit to Google Cloud for the long term and worries about being unable to move workloads later. Which characteristic of Google Cloud most directly helps reduce vendor lock-in concerns?
choices: Mandatory three-year committed use contracts that guarantee a fixed compute price in exchange for keeping every workload on the platform throughout the term
Heavy use of open-source and open-standard technologies such as Kubernetes via GKE, TensorFlow, and standard SQL, easing portability across environments
Proprietary Google-only networking protocols that function only inside Google Cloud regions and zones to deliver maximum intra-region performance for customers
A single-region design requirement that keeps every customer workload consolidated into one region for simpler operational management and lower egress pricing
questions.explanation: Google's embrace of open-source and open-standard technologies — Kubernetes (originated at Google, offered as GKE), TensorFlow, standard SQL, and similar — lets organisations build portable workloads they can run elsewhere, easing lock-in fears. Long-term commitments increase lock-in rather than reduce it; proprietary-only protocols would deepen lock-in; and a single-region mandate is not a real Google Cloud constraint and does not address portability.

questions.q: A media company collects millions of IoT sensor events per second and needs a fully managed service to ingest and buffer this real-time stream before it is processed and loaded into analytics. Which Google Cloud service fits the ingestion role?
choices: Persistent Disk, durable block storage attached to Compute Engine virtual machines for low-latency local IO from operating systems and applications
Cloud SQL, a managed relational database service designed for transactional applications on a single primary instance with synchronous read replicas
Pub/Sub, a fully managed, globally scalable messaging service for ingesting and buffering high-throughput real-time event streams asynchronously
Cloud Storage, an object store best suited to durable storage of large media files, backups, and long-term archives in regional and multi-regional buckets
questions.explanation: Pub/Sub is Google Cloud's managed, horizontally scalable messaging service built to ingest and buffer high-throughput real-time event streams, decoupling producers from downstream processors such as Dataflow. Cloud SQL is a transactional relational database, not a streaming ingestion bus; Cloud Storage holds objects and files rather than streaming messages; and Persistent Disk is block storage attached to VMs, not an event-ingestion service.
